A null state is a value the compiler's analysis carries for an expression at a point in a body. No declaration, reference, modifier or attribute records it, so an index holds no fact about the clause. TyNullStates in Nullability.cs holds the code the state moves through, for a reader.

Flow analysis is the procedure that computes those states; its inputs are ordinary expressions and its output is diagnostics. Nothing is emitted for it. TyNullStates.LengthOrZero, LengthByPattern and LengthAfterAssignment narrow by test, by pattern and by assignment for a reader to follow.

Types/ReferenceTypes.cs — THE LIBRARY SURFACE A CORPUS REFERENCES BUT NEVER DECLARES (declares=reference). Clause 5 includes Annex C in the standard by reference and C.1 further includes ISO/IEC 23271:2012 Partition IV by reference, so the normative definitions of these 110 types are two levels outside the corpus: every Annex C reference resolves to metadata, and none of them is ever declared here. This file writes `object` as the keyword and `System.Object` by framework name in one type, the highest-frequency C.2 reference of all, being the implicit base of every declared class. The measured instability is that ScipSymbols.Package() interpolates the containing assembly’s simple name and four-part version straight into the symbol string, so one unchanged source file yields `nuget System.Runtime 10.0.0.0` / `nuget System.Runtime 11.0.0.0` / `nuget System.Private.CoreLib 10.0.0.0`. What a corpus must assert instead: an identity-independent key taken from the C.5 fully-qualified name, an explicit external-reference fact so "no definition by design" is distinguishable from "index broken", assembly identity demoted to per-build provenance, and a cross-TFM golden pairing the two.

General. A conformance requirement and a permission are not constructs, and an index holds no fact about either. Recorded anyway because this heading is the licence for the whole Annex C treatment: it includes ISO/IEC 23271:2012 Partition IV by reference, so the definitions of the C.2 members are normatively outside the corpus and the absence of a definition fact for them is correct behaviour rather than a coverage gap. Its informative extension permission is sharper still — a conforming implementation may ADD INTERVENING BASE CLASSES OR INTERFACES, so the inheritance chain an indexer walks from a corpus type up to System.Object is not fixed by the standard and heritage edges through corelib cannot be asserted as language facts.

Types/ReferenceTypes.cs — C.2, Standard Library Types defined in ISO/IEC 23271 (declares=reference): 60 types over 8 namespaces, every one a metadata reference whose package coordinate comes from ContainingAssembly.Identity, so all 60 carry the measured instability. This file references the object type both as the keyword (`public static object BoxedByKeyword = 0;`) and by framework name (`public static System.Object BoxedByFrameworkName = "text";`), and the predefined-type structs are the worst case by volume — a corpus references System.Boolean/Byte/Char/Decimal/Double/Int16/Int32/Int64/IntPtr/SByte/Single/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64/UIntPtr once per keyword occurrence, so an unstable assembly identity corrupts the highest-frequency symbols in the index rather than a few edge ones. The annex’s own note flags that some structs here carry `readonly`, which postdates ISO/IEC 23271, so C.2 is not a verbatim subset of 23271 even where it defers to it.

Ranges/RngIndexType.cs — C.3, Standard Library Types not defined in ISO/IEC 23271 (declares=reference): 50 types over 7 namespaces, and this is where the measured case actually lives. System.Index is declared in C.3, not C.2, so the type that resolves to System.Runtime 10.0.0.0 / System.Runtime 11.0.0.0 / System.Private.CoreLib 10.0.0.0 is one the standard requires but ISO/IEC 23271 does not define — it has no second normative home to key against, and C.5’s `global::System.Index` is the only identity-independent name the standard offers for it. This file’s own header records that everything in it other than `RngIndexed` resolves into the core library. Its neighbours are the same shape and are all reached by operator syntax rather than by name: System.Range, ValueTuple, Span<T>/ReadOnlySpan<T>, and the four awaiter structs with INotifyCompletion/ICriticalNotifyCompletion, which every `await` binds to and which no source file names.

Expressions.Primary/PxInterpolation.cs — C.4, Format Specifications (declares=reference), and the split is the point: the interpolation itself produces ordinary references into Annex C (System.String.Format, or FormattableStringFactory.Create and FormattableString for a conversion to FormattableString) and inherits their instability, but the specifier text does not. This file writes `$"{seed:D4}"` and `$"{seed,-8:X}"`; the `D4` and `X` live inside a string token, Roslyn hands back no symbol for them, and no descriptor path can be built — so a corpus cannot assert anything about a format specifier beyond the span of the literal containing it. Recording that boundary matters because C.4 reads like an enumeration of named things and is not one. One further finding: C.4 leans throughout on System.Globalization.NumberFormatInfo and DateTimeFormatInfo, and NEITHER appears in C.2, C.3 or the C.5 name list — so a reference to NumberFormatInfo is to a type this standard names but does not require, a third category beyond "declared in corpus" and "required by Annex C".

Namespaces/Qualified/NsQualifiedAliasMember.cs — C.5, Library Type Abbreviations (declares=reference), the heading where the Annex C hazard is answered rather than restated. C.5 is the standard’s own canonical list of 107 fully-qualified names WITH the `global::` qualifier, and that canonical spelling is exactly the identity-independent key the symbol string lacks: `global::System.Index` is stable across all three measured resolutions because it names the type by the standard rather than by the assembly that happened to supply it. This file writes the `global::` reading directly — `global::System.String` and `global::Surface.Namespaces.Qualified.NsGen.NsGenNamespaceType.Clause`. BUT C.5 CANNOT BE CONSUMED AS A LITERAL WHITELIST: cdiff.py finds three defects against the C.2/C.3 code blocks — `global::System.Span` and `global::System.ReadOnlySpan` are listed with no type parameters; four entries carry a variance annotation inside what is meant to be a type name (IAsyncEnumerable<out T>, IAsyncEnumerator<out T>, IReadOnlyCollection<out T>, IReadOnlyList<out T>); and five types C.3 normatively requires are absent entirely (ValueTask, ValueTask<TResult>, CancellationToken, CancellationTokenSource, EnumeratorCancellationAttribute) — precisely the async-stream and cancellation set an `await foreach` binds to without naming.
